prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: lime green. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture, print dots and small pieces of tape.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Every surface is matte printed paper reflecting only the room light: cutouts, chips, ribbons and ground all read as photographed paper, with the same flat finish edge to edge. No glow, neon, bloom or halo anywhere.
7. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
8. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip, large, with safe margins. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: lime green.
Subjects: a paper ribbon; cutout buildings.
Opens on the steadying hand, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The previous chip flips away as the steadying hand unrolls a paper ribbon that loops around cutout buildings and ties.
Ends holding on the tied ribbon.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "WHAT CHANGES IT".

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "WHAT CHANGES IT". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: No voice, no speech, no dialogue, no lyrics. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects only; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage style video, photographed as a flat lay under soft room light from the upper left. The scene begins with <Picture 1>, featuring a magenta paper ground, a cream paper chip with the text "EXECUTION RISK" in bold black sans-serif, and black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts of folders and a hand, all with rough white torn-paper edges and small soft shadows. Immediately upon onset, the magenta ground is covered by a single, unbroken block of lime green matte paper that slides in from the left. Simultaneously, the "EXECUTION RISK" chip flips upward and away from the frame. A black-and-white halftone cutout of an anonymous paper hand (S1), characterized by a grainy photographic texture and rough white edges, remains and begins to unroll a flat matte cream paper ribbon. The camera is a Static Shot. As the ribbon unrolls, it winds and loops dynamically around several black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts of buildings, which slide into the lower two-thirds of the frame. These buildings are unmarked, with no windows or signs, possessing a stark halftone dot pattern and white torn edges. In the upper third of the frame, a new cream-colored paper chip lands with a slight overshoot, featuring the bold black sans-serif text "WHAT CHANGES IT" printed cleanly and legibly. The ribbon continues to loop and eventually ties into a neat knot around the cluster of buildings. The motion is fast and precise, settling into a stable hold for the final second. All elements maintain a matte printed paper texture with no glow or bloom, reflecting only the ambient room light.

overall_soundscape: The audio consists of tactile, diegetic paper sounds. A crisp, rhythmic paper-slap accompanies the sliding and flipping of the chips, followed by the dry, sliding friction of a paper ribbon unrolling and the subtle, sticky click of tape being pressed down.
